scope: Partial x86_64 Rust lockset server and process-query runtime integration using locally modified matching Darling inputs; no full migration claim.
upstream_gaps_and_bugs_fixed: lockset_create and other lockset APIs were unconditional failure stubs; now real Mach ports, ownership, wait/handoff, unstable recovery and lifecycle behavior
proc_info LISTPIDS was unsupported; now namespace-aware enumeration and filters
proc_name returned loader name instead of registered executable basename
legacy PIDLISTTHREADS wrote before checking short buffer capacity
legacy region query copied uninitialized data on no matching region; Rust initializes records and reports an error
new_integration_bugs_found_and_fixed: thread/task cleanup delayed until final reference deallocation; now dying/exec hooks
interrupted handoff could transfer ownership but report aborted
raw procfs queries used wrong virtual root namespace
vchroot followed procfs magic links twice
overlay maps device identity disagreed with guest stat
C bridge port slot type punning and unsynchronized priority read

checks.cargo_xtask_check: pass: formatting, strict Clippy and workspace tests
checks.darwin_runtime_staging: pass; integrated process.o byte-identical to app-tested object
gui_apps: Cocotron TextEditor: actual XTest typing and manually verified screenshots, both kernel variants
Cocoa Calculator fixture: mapped window, button actions assert42, both kernel variants
checks.lockset_guest_probes: ownership, invalid IDs/policy, thread/task death, unstable recovery, blocked destroy,100portlifecycles,cross-process Machsendrights,and retained-task exec retirement: pass both kernel variants
checks.process_guest_probe: filters and negative filter, byte counts, short/negative buffers/canaries, threads, vnode layouts/metadata/ownership, fd path/list, cwd/root, open-file and mmap-only path lookup: pass

comparison_interpretation: Both app variants use the new Rust lockset server. Original means original client kernel. Original kernel still fails libproc; Rust fixes it. cfbridge has one explicitly normalized timestamped NSLog line in both. Harness returns1 for strict mismatches; none hidden.
limits: Most Darling code remains C/C++/assembly; unported process query flavors delegate to legacy C.
Selected x86_64 locally modified runtime only; clean pinned full-runtime and i386 execution pending.
FIFO and fixed-priority are documented lockset policies; fixed-priority uses enqueue-time priority, not live reprioritization.
Unlinked overlay mappings cannot always recover guest-visible device identity.
No arbitrary GUI app, cancellation, or exhaustive scheduler-race compatibility claim.
environment: New short prefixes, private unprivileged user/mount/PID namespaces, private server bind. All test prefixes shut down. Installed kernel/server hashes unchanged; task-owned Xephyr stopped; existing user prefix untouched.
